extraFields.label: Community fees (comunidad)
extraFields.help: Monthly fee to your building’s owners’ association. Tenants usually have it included in the rent; leave it empty if so.

single.note: Estimate; tenants usually pay it inside the rent. Cuantomecuesta gives a €30–250/month range for owners

suburban.note: Estimate within the €30–250 owner range (Cuantomecuesta); pools and lifts push it up

extraFields.label: Private health insurance
extraFields.help: Monthly premium for private health cover (e.g. Sanitas, Adeslas, DKV), if you have it.

single.note: Estimate; optional, many rely on public health care

localTips.title: Check PVPC against a fixed-price tariff
localTips.why: The regulated PVPC follows wholesale prices hour by hour; depending on your habits a fixed-price free-market tariff may be cheaper, or the other way round.
tips: Compare with the CNMC comparison tool using your last bills.
Lower your contracted power (potencia) if you never trip the fuse.
Run the washing machine and dishwasher in the off-peak hours (00:00–08:00 and weekends).

pct.note: Estimate; not from a cited study

localTips.title: Get out of revolving credit
localTips.why: Revolving cards charge around 22–24% TAE, and low fixed payments can keep you in debt for years.
tips: Switch the card from "pago aplazado" to paying the full balance each month.
Ask your bank for a personal loan (~7% average) to clear the card.
If your card charged far above the market average when you signed, ask a consumer association (OCU, Asufin) whether it may be usurious.

pct.note: Estimate: share of card interest avoided by moving to a ~7% personal loan

localTips.title: Use the subsidised monthly pass
localTips.why: Regional and state-subsidised passes (abono joven, abono único) are much cheaper than single tickets for regular commuters.
tips: Check your region’s monthly pass and the youth discount if you are under 26.
Compare it with what you spend on single tickets and parking.
Ask your employer about tax-free transport cards (tarjeta transporte).
